chunks: surely the remembrance of death has kept me away from fun and play while obliviousness about the next world has prevented him from speaking truth.
He has not sworn allegiance to Mu‘āwiyah without purpose; but has beforehand got him to agree that he will have to pay its price, and gave him an award for forsaking religion.
ai.seo_question: How did Amr ibn al-As justify his political allegiance to Mu'awiya in contrast to his personal piety?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Amr ibn al-As articulates the psychological mechanism of his political pragmatism, contrasting his own 'remembrance of death' (dhikr al-mawt) which curbed his frivolity, with Mu'awiya's 'forgetfulness of the Hereafter' which eroded his truthfulness. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between spiritual awareness and political action, where allegiance is often conditional upon the preservation of core religious identity. The 'specific compensation' (atiyyah) mentioned underscores the concept of temporary compromise (istidraaj) rather than permanent apostasy, a key theme in evaluating the Sahaba's political choices.
